google-gemini__gemini-cli@0fa1bd7.pr_summary: Fix for #8077 (saving settings rewrote the whole settings.json, dropping comments and writing env-var references out as resolved plaintext). Adds comment-json and utils/commentJson.ts: updateSettingsFilePreservingFormat parses the existing file, deep-merges the in-memory settings into it (applyUpdates), restores recorded $VAR references (restoreEnvVarReferences) and stringifies with 2-space indent; trackEnvVarMappings records settings paths whose original value was exactly a $VAR/${VAR}. loadSettings records mappings per scope around resolveEnvVarsInObject and LoadedSettings.setValue passes them to saveSettings, which (after the existing migrateSettingsToV1 conversion) writes through the new helper.

defects.title: Merge-only save never deletes keys: removed MCP servers (and replaced fields) persist on disk
defects.statement: applyUpdates (commentJson.ts:52-80) starts from the parsed file and only adds/overwrites keys present in the in-memory settings, recursing into nested objects; keys deleted in memory are never removed from the file. `gemini mcp remove` does `delete mcpServers[name]; settings.setValue(scope, 'mcpServers', mcpServers)` (commands/mcp/remove.ts:30-32), so the server stays in settings.json and reappears on restart while the CLI reports it removed; re-adding a server with a different transport merges into the old object, leaving stale command/args beside httpUrl. Before the PR the whole object was written with JSON.stringify, so deletions took effect.
defects.evidence: commentJson.ts:56 `const result = current;` then :58-77 loop over `Object.entries(updates)` assigning `result[key] = ...`; nothing deletes keys absent from updates. remove.ts: `delete mcpServers[name]; settings.setValue(settingsScope, 'mcpServers', mcpServers);`. Base saveSettings wrote `JSON.stringify(settingsToSave, null, 2)`.
defects.notes: Must say the new save merges and never removes keys that were deleted in memory (mcp remove / replaced nested objects). R11 (arrays replaced wholesale) and R9 (mutating the parsed object) do not count.

defects.title: Env references embedded in a larger string ("Bearer $TOKEN") are not tracked and are written back resolved
defects.statement: resolveEnvVarsInString (utils/envVarResolver.ts:20-28) substitutes $VAR/${VAR} anywhere inside a string, but trackEnvVarMappings records a mapping only when the whole original string matches the anchored /^\$(?:(\w+)|{([^}]+)})$/ (commentJson.ts:152). A value like an MCP header "Authorization": "Bearer $API_TOKEN" or "${BASE_URL}/api" is resolved at load, not tracked, and the next save of that scope (any setValue, e.g. /settings theme toggle) writes the resolved secret into settings.json - the leak #8077 is about, left open for the common header/URL case.
defects.evidence: commentJson.ts:152 `const envVarPattern = /^\$(?:(\w+)|{([^}]+)})$/;` vs envVarResolver.ts `const envVarRegex = /\$(?:(\w+)|{([^}]+)})/g;` used with value.replace, doc example `resolveEnvVarsInString("Token: $API_KEY")`. saveSettings passes the resolved settingsFile.settings as updates.
defects.notes: Must say partial/embedded references are resolved but not tracked/restored, so they are saved in plaintext. R13 (support default-value/nested syntax) does not count. Graded medium, not high: before the PR every value (whole or embedded reference) was written back resolved, so the embedded case is a gap in the fix, not a regression, the same class and grade as D3 and D4.

defects.title: Env references inside arrays (e.g. MCP args) are tracked but never restored, so they are saved resolved
defects.statement: trackEnvVarMappings recurses into arrays (for...in yields index keys, commentJson.ts:146,162-168) and resolveEnvVarsInObject resolves array items, but restoreEnvVarsRecursive only descends into non-array objects (commentJson.ts:117-123) and applyUpdates replaces arrays wholesale with the resolved in-memory array (:76). "args": ["--api-key", "$API_KEY"] is therefore written back with the secret in plaintext on the next save of that scope.
defects.evidence: commentJson.ts:117-121 `} else if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)) { restoreEnvVarsRecursive(...) }`; :162 `else if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null)` includes arrays when tracking; envVarResolver.ts maps arrays item by item.
defects.notes: Must say env references inside arrays are not restored (leak). C16 also mentions arrays but is filed under D2 (its lead point). R11 on array merge granularity does not count.

defects.title: Env mappings are recorded on V2 paths but the saved object is converted to V1, so references for migrated keys leak
defects.statement: loadAndMigrate migrates V1 files to V2 in memory (settings.ts:576-600) before the mappings are captured on the V2 object (:663-683). With MIGRATE_V2_OVERWRITE = false (:60), saveSettings always runs migrateSettingsToV1 (:731-735) before calling the updater, so every key in MIGRATION_MAP is written under its V1 name while the mapping paths are V2 (e.g. ['tools','discoveryCommand'] vs top-level toolDiscoveryCommand, ['model','name'] vs model). restoreEnvVarsRecursive never matches them, and saving any setting writes the resolved env value in plaintext. Only mcpServers (same path in both shapes) is protected.
defects.evidence: settings.ts:60 `const MIGRATE_V2_OVERWRITE = false;`; :731-735 `if (!MIGRATE_V2_OVERWRITE) { settingsToSave = migrateSettingsToV1(...) }`; MIGRATION_MAP :117 `toolDiscoveryCommand: 'tools.discoveryCommand'`; mappings built from the migrated objects at :663-683; commentJson.ts:112-115 looks up `fullPath.join('.')` of the V1 structure.
defects.notes: Must say the mapping paths (V2) do not match the V1-converted structure written by saveSettings, so env references for non-mcpServers keys are lost/leaked.

defects.title: Saving into a V2-format file adds V1 keys beside the old nested values, and the old value wins on reload
defects.statement: saveSettings converts to V1 (settings.ts:731-735) and the updater now MERGES into the parsed file instead of replacing it. For a hand-written V2 file with {"ui": {"theme": "A"}}, changing the theme writes a top-level "theme": "B" but leaves ui.theme = "A". On reload needsMigration sees the V1 key, migrateSettingsToV2 sets ui.theme = B and then carries over the unrecognized original `ui` object (settings.ts:251-254), overwriting it with {theme: "A"}; the edit is lost. Before the PR the whole file was rewritten in V1 so no duplicate existed.
defects.evidence: migrateSettingsToV2: `for (const [oldKey, newPath] of Object.entries(MIGRATION_MAP)) { if (flatKeys.has(oldKey)) { setNestedProperty(v2Settings, newPath, ...); flatKeys.delete(oldKey); } }` then `for (const remainingKey of flatKeys) { v2Settings[remainingKey] = flatSettings[remainingKey]; }` - `ui` remains in flatKeys and replaces the freshly set ui object. applyUpdates merges `theme` without touching `ui`.
defects.notes: Must say V1-converted save merged into a V2 file leaves the old nested value, which overrides the edit on next load (or duplicates V1/V2 keys with the stale one winning). Plain 'keys are not deleted' (D1) is a different defect.

defects.title: A deliberately changed value at an env-backed path is silently reverted to the $VAR reference on save
defects.statement: restoreEnvVarsRecursive (commentJson.ts:114-116) restores the recorded reference whenever the path matches and the current value is any string, never comparing with mapping.resolvedValue (recorded at :159, read nowhere), and the mappings captured at load are reused by every setValue (settings.ts:421-422). If a user replaces an env-backed value (e.g. `gemini mcp add` re-adding a server with `-e API_KEY=newkey` where the file had "$API_KEY"), the file keeps "$VAR" and the new value is lost on restart.
defects.evidence: commentJson.ts:115 `if (envVarReference && typeof value === 'string') { (obj as Record<string, unknown>)[key] = envVarReference; }`; EnvVarMapping.resolvedValue set at :159 and unused.
defects.notes: Must say restoration ignores whether the value was changed (resolvedValue unused / stale mappings). R3 (non-string resolved values) does not count.

defects.title: Comments inside arrays are still dropped on every save
defects.statement: applyUpdates replaces every array in the parsed file with the plain in-memory array (commentJson.ts:63-76, arrays take the `result[key] = value` branch). comment-json stores comments on array items as symbol properties of the parsed CommentArray, so any comment inside an array (e.g. a commented-out arg or excluded tool) is removed whenever any setting in that scope is saved - the comment preservation the PR claims is incomplete for arrays.
defects.evidence: commentJson.ts:66 `!Array.isArray(value)` excludes arrays from the merge branch; :76 `result[key] = value;` assigns the plain resolved array from settingsFile.settings (built via JSON.parse(stripJsonComments(...)) and resolveEnvVarsInObject, so it carries no comment metadata).
defects.notes: Must say comments attached to array elements are lost because arrays are replaced wholesale. R11 (arrays replaced instead of element-wise merge, no mention of comments) does not count.

excluded.reason: Claim: the constructor parameter `migratedInMemorScopes` is misspelled. The identifier pre-exists this PR (only context lines here); a naming nit, not a defect.
Claim: define a named type alias instead of `ReturnType<typeof trackEnvVarMappings>` in the Map. Readability preference with no functional consequence.

Claim: restoration only happens for string values, so env vars resolving to numbers/booleans/objects would be saved resolved. resolveEnvVarsInString always returns a string and tracking requires both values to be strings, so a resolved env value is never a non-string; the premise is unreachable.

Claim: updateSettingsFilePreservingFormat should validate that filePath is a string and updates an object. It is a typed internal helper with a single caller passing a path and the settings object; a runtime-validation request, not a defect.

Claim: add type checking before casting the parsed file to Record<string, unknown>. loadSettings already rejects non-object settings files, so on reachable paths the parsed content is an object; speculative.

Claim: on parse failure the function logs and returns instead of throwing. A file that fails comment-json parsing would already have failed loadSettings; only an external edit between load and save reaches it, and saveSettings itself only logs errors as before.
Claim: stringify(..., null, 2) forces 2-space indentation, changing tab/4-space files. The previous code also wrote JSON.stringify(settingsToSave, null, 2), so formatting is not made worse; cosmetic.
Claim: writeFileSync lacks handling for EACCES/ENOENT. The only caller saveSettings wraps the call in try/catch and logs, exactly as before.
Claim: applyUpdates mutates the object passed in rather than a deep copy. The mutated object is the freshly parsed file content local to updateSettingsFilePreservingFormat; no side effect escapes.

Claim: Object.entries in applyUpdates introduces prototype-pollution risk. applyUpdates explicitly skips __proto__/constructor/prototype and Object.entries yields only own enumerable keys; no pollution path exists.

Claim: applyUpdates replaces arrays wholesale instead of updating individual elements. Replacing a settings array with the saved array is the correct save semantics; element-wise merge would be wrong. It names neither the env-var leak (D3) nor the comment loss (D7).

Claim: joining mapping paths with '.' is ambiguous when a key contains a dot. Tracking and restoring use the same join, so a mis-restore needs both a dotted key and a nested path spelling the identical string with an env reference; contrived.

Claim: the env pattern should support default values or nested references. The resolver itself supports only $VAR/${VAR}, so there is nothing more to track; it does not state the real gap (embedded references, D2).
Claim: forcing 2-space indentation reformats tab/4-space files on an unrelated edit. The base code already rewrote the file with JSON.stringify(..., null, 2), so this is not a regression; cosmetic.

Claim: an unrelated setting edit reserializes and reformats the whole file (fixed indent, LF). Same as base behaviour (full JSON.stringify rewrite); formatting preference, not a defect introduced here.
Claim: the single-setting save writes a fully reserialized snapshot, reformatting unchanged content. Same root as C24; base also rewrote the entire file; cosmetic.

Claim: if the settings file disappears between load and save, the new-file branch writes resolved updates without restoring references. Mappings exist only for files that existed at load, so this needs the file deleted mid-session; contrived, and base behaviour wrote resolved values too.
Claim: the !existsSync branch bypasses envVarMappings, so recreating a deleted file writes the resolved token. Same contrived deleted-between-load-and-save scenario as C5.

Claim: the new-file branch writes settingsToSave with JSON.stringify before applying mappings, persisting resolved secrets if the file was removed or config was in-memory migrated. Migrated-in-memory scopes still have their file on disk (existing-file branch); only a mid-session deletion reaches this; contrived.
Claim: the parse-error log should include filePath. Diagnostic-message improvement; the parse-failure path is only reachable if the file is corrupted after a successful load.

Claim: returning on parse failure reports success to setValue although nothing was written. Only reachable if the file became unparseable after loadSettings parsed it; contrived, and saveSettings only ever logged failures.

Claim: the prototype-pollution test builds `__proto__` via an object literal, so it sets the prototype rather than an own key and never exercises the guard. A test-quality observation; the guard itself is correct and no runtime defect results.
Claim: same as C19 - the malicious update's object-literal `__proto__` is not an own key so the test would pass without the guard. Test-coverage request, not a defect in shipped behaviour.

Claims flattening mapping paths with join('.') lets an MCP server literally named 'foo.bar' collide with a nested foo->bar path so one env reference is restored under the other's name. Same as R12: tracking and restoring use the same join, so a mis-restore needs a dotted key AND a nested path spelling the identical string, both env-backed; contrived.

Claims the helper's create-file branch (commentJson.ts:24-26) writes updates without applying the env mappings, persisting resolved secrets in a newly created file. Same as C5/C7: mappings exist only for files that existed at load, so a mapped value reaches the create branch only if the file is deleted mid-session; contrived, and a file absent at load has no $VAR references to restore.

defects.title: http-server example: _Errors and _Health tests request fresh random ports where no server listens

Now each test calls testutil.NewServerConfigs(t), which allocates new ports, but only the first test starts main(). TestIntegration_SimpleAPIServer_Errors (main_test.go:70, request :99) and _Health (:126, request :138) target ports nothing listens on: c.Do errors with nil resp, so Errors panics at io.ReadAll(resp.Body) (:109) and Health fails require.NoError.

defects.title: Test_AddDuplicateHTTPService lost its METRICS_PORT isolation: New() now checks default port 2121 and Fatalf's the test binary if it is taken

Claim (item 5): in examples/using-http-service/main_test.go the package-level `port` is no longer assigned while handler tests at lines 76/101 still build URLs with it, pointing at localhost:0. defects.title: lora_dtype default 'bf32' is not an offered option, so Train LoRA fails with default values
defects.statement: nodes_train.py:344-347 declares lora_dtype choices ['bf16','fp32'] but default 'bf32'. execution.py:736 combo validation rejects a value not in the list ('Value not in list'), and even if it passed, node_helpers.string_to_torch_dtype('bf32') returns None (node_helpers.py:46-52), so the adapter .to(lora_dtype) calls get None.

defects.title: Only one random batch is ever trained on; the rest of the dataset is ignored
defects.statement: train() samples `indices = torch.randperm(num_images)[:batch_size]` and VAE-encodes that batch once (nodes_train.py:381-386) before the loop; every step at :503-514 reuses the same `encoded` tensor. With more images than batch_size (default 1) all other images are never seen.

defects.title: Selecting an existing LoRA whose filename lacks the '<n>_steps_' pattern crashes with ValueError
defects.statement: existing_steps = int(existing_lora.split('_steps_')[0].split('_')[-1]) (nodes_train.py:403) is applied to any file from the full loras list (:349). Ordinary LoRA names, and this node's own output saved without steps ('{prefix}_{date}_lora.safetensors', :599), raise ValueError and abort training.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:403; options from folder_paths.get_filename_list('loras') at :349.
defects.notes: Must name the filename-based int parse of the step count failing for non-matching names.

defects.title: SaveLoRA writes to a CWD-relative 'models/loras/' path instead of the configured loras directory
defects.statement: SaveLoRA.save builds f'models/loras/{prefix}_...safetensors' (nodes_train.py:599/601) relative to the process working directory, ignoring folder_paths (models_dir derives from base_path/--base-directory, folder_paths.py:18-30). Started from another directory or with --base-directory / extra model paths, the save raises FileNotFoundError or lands where the loras list (and Train LoRA's existing_lora) never sees it.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:599-602 literal 'models/loras/'; folder_paths.py base_path from args.base_directory or dirname(__file__).
defects.notes: Must say the output path is hardcoded/relative to CWD rather than via folder_paths. Path-traversal via prefix is a separate defect (D5).

defects.title: User-supplied filename prefixes are written without path containment (SaveLoRA and Plot Loss Graph)
defects.statement: SaveLoRA interpolates the workflow STRING `prefix` into the output path (nodes_train.py:599/601) and LossGraphNode joins `filename_prefix` onto the temp dir (:680-681) with no containment check; a prefix like '../../x' writes files outside the intended directory. The repo's existing save path (folder_paths.get_save_image_path, folder_paths.py:387-391) refuses paths outside the output folder, so these nodes bypass the established guard for API-submitted workflows.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:599 `f"models/loras/{prefix}_..."`; :681 `os.path.join(self.output_dir, f"{filename_prefix}_{date}.png")`; folder_paths.py:387 commonpath check used by other save nodes.
defects.notes: Must say the prefix / filename_prefix can contain traversal components and escape the destination directory. Either site counts. Not: the hardcoded relative path (D4). Not: the folder input of Load Image Dataset (combo-validated).

defects.title: Resuming from an existing LoRA drops its trained 1-D weight diffs and bias diffs
defects.statement: When existing_lora is set only >=2-D weights are restored through the adapter loader; 1-D weight diffs ('{n}.diff') and bias diffs ('{n}.diff_b') are always recreated as zeros (nodes_train.py:443-460), so the previously trained values are discarded and the re-saved LoRA loses them.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:444-446 and :454-456 torch.zeros regardless of existing_weights; the trainer itself saves '{n}.diff'/'{n}.diff_b' (:451/:458), which comfy/lora.py:72-82 reads at inference.
defects.notes: Must say existing diff/diff_b (bias or 1-D) values are not loaded on resume.

defects.title: Resuming misreads the existing LoRA's alpha, changing its effective scale
defects.statement: Alpha is looked up as f'{key}.alpha' with key='{n}.weight' (nodes_train.py:411,414), but LoRA files and this trainer's own output store '{n}.alpha' (named_parameters 'alpha' at :437-438; comfy/lora.py:41). So a stored non-1.0 alpha is replaced by 1.0; and a LoRA with no alpha (inference scale 1.0, lora.py:169-172) resumes with scale alpha/rank = 1/rank. Either way the resumed adapter no longer reproduces the checkpoint's weights.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:414 `existing_weights.get(f"{key}.alpha", 1.0)`; comfy/lora.py:41 `alpha_name = "{}.alpha".format(x)`; weight_adapter/lora.py:169-172 alpha None -> 1.0.
defects.notes: Either the wrong key ('.weight.alpha') or the missing-alpha → 1/rank scale mismatch counts.

defects.title: Resuming a DoRA / reshape-weight LoRA ignores dora_scale and reshape
defects.statement: LoraDiff unpacks dora_scale and reshape (lora.py:18) but __call__ (lora.py:42-52) applies only w + scale*diff, unlike calculate_weight which applies weight_decompose and pad_tensor_to_shape (lora.py:163-190); in addition the trainer looks dora_scale up under '{n}.weight.dora_scale' (nodes_train.py:415-417) rather than '{n}.dora_scale'. A DoRA LoRA resumed for training therefore loses its magnitude decomposition and changes effective weights.
defects.evidence: lora.py:18 `mat1, mat2, alpha, mid, dora_scale, reshape = weights` and neither used in __call__.
defects.notes: Must say DoRA scale (or reshape) is ignored/lost in the training conversion.

defects.title: Resume looks up existing LoRA keys only by raw module name, silently starting fresh for alias-keyed files
defects.statement: The trainer calls adapter_cls.load(n, existing_weights, ...) with the raw module name n (nodes_train.py:418-421), while inference maps accepted aliases such as 'lora_unet_...' to model keys (comfy/lora.py:180-204). A LoRA in those formats matches nothing, so every module takes the fresh-init branch (:432-436) with no warning, yet existing_steps is still added to the returned step count.

defects.title: Resuming from a conv (LoCon/tucker) LoRA crashes in LoraDiff construction
defects.statement: LoraDiff.__init__ (lora.py:21-36) picks the conv class with index mid.ndim-2 (Conv3d for a 4-D mid), constructs Conv layers without kernel_size, and calls layer(mid, rank) passing a tensor as in_channels, so any LoRA with lora_mid raises TypeError; a conv LoRA without mid has 4-D up/down tensors that cannot copy_ into the 2-D Linear weights (:30-33). The trainer calls to_train() on these (nodes_train.py:431).
defects.evidence: lora.py:35 `self.lora_mid = layer(mid, rank, bias=False)`; :22-27 `(Conv1d, Conv2d, Conv3d)[mid.ndim - 2]`; :30-31 no kernel_size.
defects.notes: Any of: tensor passed as channel count, wrong Conv class for mid dims, missing kernel_size, 4-D up/down into Linear. Not R8 (tucker reshape).

defects.title: Resuming from a non-LoRA adapter file (LoHa/LoKr/OFT/BOFT/GLoRA) raises NotImplementedError
defects.statement: The resume loop tries every registered adapter class (nodes_train.py:418-423) and unconditionally calls existing_adapter.to_train() (:431), but only LoRAAdapter implements to_train; WeightAdapterBase.to_train raises NotImplementedError (base.py:18-19).
defects.evidence: base.py:18-19; lora.py:77-78 is the only to_train.
defects.notes: Must say non-LoRA adapter types reach to_train and fail. R6 (create_train on subclasses) is a near-miss and does not count.

defects.statement: In TrainSampler.sample (nodes_train.py:46-51) a RuntimeError from loss_fn is caught, conditionally logged and not re-raised; loss.backward() then raises UnboundLocalError, masking the real error. The matched 'does not require grad' message comes from backward(), not the loss call.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:46-51.
defects.notes: Must say the exception is swallowed and 'loss' is then undefined.

defects.statement: LossGraphNode.plot_loss scales by (max_loss - min_loss) (nodes_train.py:637-638); steps min is 1 (:293), so a one-step run or constant loss raises ZeroDivisionError.
defects.evidence: nodes_train.py:637-638; steps min 1 at :293.

defects.statement: patch() replaces forward on modules of mp.model.diffusion_model (nodes_train.py:482-483); model.clone() shares the underlying model.
